explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/694: with f_max(n), f_min(n) the largest and smallest m with φ(m) = n, investigate max_{n ≤ x, n ∈ φ(ℕ)} f_max(n)/f_min(n); the page records the result (GPT-5.5 Pro, prompted by Price) that this equals (e^γ + o(1)) log log x. The Lean statement takes any fmax, fmin agreeing with IsGreatest/IsLeast of the totient fibre on every n in the image of φ, and asserts ∃ o → 0 such that eventually sSup {fmax n / fmin n : n ≤ x, n ∈ range φ} = (exp γ + o x)·log log x. The set is finite and nonempty, so sSup is the maximum. Mathlib's φ(0) = 0 adds n = 0 with fibre {0} and ratio 0/0 = 0, which does not affect the maximum; n = 1 gives 2/1 as on the page. The existential o with equality is the standard encoding of (e^γ + o(1)). Faithful formalisation of the stated answer.
